name: LifeOSBoard
tagline: A browser dashboard that bundles tasks, habits, goals, a focus timer, and notes into one screen.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is five well-understood widgets sharing a layout: a task list, a habit grid, a goal tracker, a Pomodoro timer, and a notes pane. None of them need a server, a model, or anyone else's data, and the whole thing already lives in a browser tab. An agent can produce a local-first version with IndexedDB persistence in a single session, and the result will be genuinely usable for one person. What you are actually buying from the product is the fact that someone already made the layout decisions and keeps it synced across your devices. If you want it on your phone and your laptop with the same state, the DIY version gets noticeably more annoying.
coreLoopDIY: A single-page local app with tabs or panels for tasks, habits with streaks, goals with progress, a focus timer, and markdown notes, all persisted in the browser.
requirements: Somewhere to host the static build, or just run it locally
Optional: a file export habit so you do not lose everything when you clear site data
whatYouLose: Cross-device sync, unless you bolt on a backend or sync files yourself
A mobile-shaped experience that does not feel like a desktop app squeezed sideways
Notifications and reminders that fire when the tab is closed
Someone else's taste on layout, spacing, and which widgets deserve the top of the screen
Backups you did not have to think about
moatNotes: The hard part of an all-in-one dashboard is restraint, not features. A DIY build tends to grow into the complicated system the product exists to avoid.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value is being handed a finished opinion. Anyone who wants tasks plus habits plus a timer in one place has usually already tried building it in Notion and quit, so paying a few dollars for a dashboard that opens and works is cheaper than another weekend of yak shaving. Sync across phone and laptop is the other half: once a few months of habit streaks live in it, moving is a real cost, and nobody wants their streak data trapped in a browser tab they might accidentally clear.
notes: The honest risk is not that the build fails, it is that you keep adding panels until you have rebuilt the thing you were avoiding.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal life dashboard as a single static web app. No backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no third-party APIs.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all persistence
- date-fns for date math
- No router library, use local state for view switching

Layout: one screen, responsive grid. Four panels on desktop, stacked on mobile. A thin header with today's date and a theme toggle (light/dark, persisted).

Panels to build:
1. Tasks: add, edit inline, complete, delete, drag to reorder. Fields: title, optional due date, optional priority (low/med/high). Filters: today, upcoming, all, completed. Completed items collapse into a count.
2. Habits: user defines habits with a target cadence (daily or N times per week). Show a 7 day check grid plus a current streak and best streak per habit. Clicking a cell toggles that day.
3. Goals: title, optional target number and current number, optional target date. Render a progress bar. Goals can be archived, not just deleted.
4. Focus timer: configurable work/break lengths, default 25/5. Start, pause, reset, and a session counter for today. Log each completed session with a timestamp and optionally a linked task id. Use a document title update and an audible chime on completion; do not request notification permission.
5. Notes: a list of notes with title and markdown body, rendered with marked. Autosave with a 500ms debounce. Simple text search across titles and bodies.

Data rules:
- One Dexie database, versioned schema, typed tables for tasks, habits, habitEntries, goals, notes, focusSessions, settings.
- Export all data as a single JSON file and import it back with a confirm step that warns about overwriting.
- Seed an empty state with short helper text in each panel, not fake demo data.

Quality bar:
- Keyboard: Enter adds a task from the input, Escape cancels an inline edit.
- No layout shift when panels are empty.
- All state survives a hard refresh.

Deliver a README with run and build commands and a one paragraph note on where the data lives and how to back it up. Do not add auth, sync, sharing, or any cloud service.
